A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Localize-and-Stitch, with matching authors, method, and core experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial relocation and reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original model-merging experiments on RoBERTa-base, GPT2-XL, and CLIP, alongside grafting, sparsity, runtime, and continual-learning analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and reports additional Consensus comparisons, task-similarity experiments, sparsity controls, and continual-training results.

M1.justification: The sigmoid-mask objective with L1 regularization, binary rounding, dataless magnitude selection, and overlap-averaging stitching remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 is relocated; expanded comparisons with other localization methods do not introduce a new component.

E1.justification: The twelve language tasks, eight vision datasets, GPT2-XL evaluation and surrogate datasets, and ImageNet evaluation are retained. The new similar/dissimilar groups reorganize existing tasks for analysis. Continual learning already appears in v1.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated Consensus TA and Consensus TIES comparators across the RoBERTa, CLIP, and GPT2-XL benchmarks, plus runtime and continual-learning comparisons. Figure 9 also adds sequential continual training, absent from v1 Table 10. This substantially strengthens comparison with closely related approaches.

E3.justification: V2 adds normalized merging metrics and uses normalized accuracy in the continual-learning plot. New experiments specify similar/dissimilar task groups and matched 1% sparsity controls. The runtime scaling-factor grid changes from 0.1–0.9 to 0.1–1.0, although the old evaluation counts and runtimes remain; this establishes a reported setting change, not a confirmed rerun.

E4.justification: New Table 6 tests whether merging advantages depend on task similarity. Appendix D adds Consensus hyperparameter-to-sparsity analysis and comparisons at matched 1% sparsity, testing localization quality beyond sparsity alone. The existing continual-learning analysis gains additional comparators; earlier sparsity, data-availability, grafting, and TIES analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests for its experiments. V2's normalized metrics do not constitute uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Original benchmark scores are retained, including Localize-and-Stitch averages of 0.759 for RoBERTa, 0.799 for CLIP, and 0.367 for GPT2-XL. V2 adds substantial results: Consensus TA/TIES score 0.715/0.695 on RoBERTa and 0.737/0.748 on CLIP, alongside new task-group, matched-sparsity, runtime, and continual-training outcomes. These are added comparisons, not improved scores for the unchanged method.

T1.justification: The localization formulation, sparsity relaxation, stitching equations, and shared-pretraining assumption are unchanged. The grafting formulation expanded in v2 Section 3.2 already appears in v1 Appendix C. Added comparator summaries and the standard normalized-score formula introduce no new theoretical argument, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: sparse localization and stitching reduce interference, support compression, preserve pretrained knowledge, and enable efficient continual composition. Additional experiments support these existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the task-group experiment as evidence that its advantage emerges with conflicting skills, and suggests independently finetuning then merging as an alternative to sequential finetuning. Conversely, v1 Appendix G's explicit discussion of unresolved theory and the remaining single-task performance gap is removed. The common-initialization requirement remains in Section 2.

D1.justification: V2 newly identifies MMLU as 5-shot accuracy and TruthfulQA as MC2, provides Consensus tuning details, and changes the code repository pointer from the yifei-he namespace to uiuctml. Core hardware, checkpoints, optimization hyperparameters, and localization settings remain unchanged. The metric labels clarify existing experiments rather than establish changed execution.

R1.justification: Wang et al.'s localization work, briefly cited in v1, becomes an explicitly distinguished and evaluated competitor with a dedicated appendix. Section 5 substantially expands positioning through pruning, same-task model fusion, and mixture-of-experts literature, including a substantive explanation of pruning versus localization. Theory references accompanying the removed limitations also disappear.

P1.justification: Most core prose and the six-section narrative remain intact. V2 expands method comparisons using existing appendix material, swaps the vision and decoder subsections, promotes continual learning into Section 4.4, and reorganizes appendices. Publication metadata and citation style also change.

P2.justification: V2 adopts TMLR formatting and substantially reorganizes displays: a combined summary table replaces the main-text language and vision tables, whose detailed rows move to Appendix A. V1's continual-learning table becomes a two-panel Figure 9 with additional curves. New analysis tables, clarified metric labels, and a relocated algorithm further change presentation.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses a meaningful evaluation gap by directly comparing against the already-cited Consensus methods and adding matched-sparsity and task-similarity controls. These additions strengthen assessment of the unchanged method, while clearer metric labels improve transparency. The net gain is tempered by removal of v1's explicit limitations and the inconsistent runtime-grid description, supporting a limited overall improvement.
